findings.statement: CA9 is tumour-cell intrinsic: RCC cells hold this share of tumour transcripts [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976], and the paired pseudobulk tumour-vs-proximal-tubule fold change is [gene=CA9; type=sc_tumor_vs_pt; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; log2fc=7.739]. Purity extrapolation and TCGA replication agree, so this is a tumour marker rather than stromal signal, though DepMap shows no dependency.

In Visium sections, high-CA9 spots are surrounded by RCC-rich neighbours (log2 enrichment [gene=CA9; type=spatial_neighborhood; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=RCC; log2_enrichment=0.381]), with a smaller macrophage enrichment; the composition-corrected in situ expresser is RCC, consistent with the single-cell attribution.

The AlphaFold CA9 model has a mean pLDDT of [gene=CA9; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=76.56]; the top cavity has a volume in cubic angstrom of [gene=CA9; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; volume_a3=126.8] and detected cavities recover a fraction of experimental ligand-contact residues (recall [gene=CA9; type=ligand_site_validation; source=PDBe-KB ligand sites (experimental holo structures); recall=0.5]). This is a descriptive monomer heuristic only; it does not identify degrons or predict degradation.

CD70 is highest in RCC cells in the single-cell data, expressed by a minority to about half of them, but T cells and Tregs also carry some signal, so it is tumour-enriched rather than exclusive. TCGA replication and a positive purity-extrapolated fold change support tumour-cell expression; clinical-stage CD70 antibodies already exist, so it is not novel.

KDR transcripts are almost entirely endothelial (share of tumour transcripts [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.951]); RCC cells contribute essentially nothing in situ. KDR is a microenvironment (anti-angiogenic) target, not a tumour-cell target.

EPAS1 (HIF-2 alpha) transcripts are not mainly in RCC cells: endothelium holds this share of tumour transcripts [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.365] while the percentage of RCC cells with a UMI is only [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=4.9], which is likely a detection limit of scRNA-seq for this transcript; bulk RNA is therefore a mixed signal.

CD74 is an immune-cell gene: macrophages hold this share of tumour transcripts [gene=CD74; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Macrophage; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.436] and cDC, B and pDC cells express it in nearly all cells, so any bulk upregulation reflects infiltration, not tumour cells.

CXCR4 is carried by lymphocytes: cytotoxic T cells hold this share of tumour transcripts [gene=CXCR4; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=CD8_T; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.563], with helper T, B and pDC cells also high; it is an immune microenvironment target, not tumour-intrinsic.

COL23A1 (tumour track, first-in-class status): RCC cells hold this share of its tumour transcripts [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881], the fold change extrapolated to a pure tumour stays high [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88], it replicates in TCGA, has no adverse-survival signal, few ccrcc papers and no clinical drug, is annotated as a cell-membrane protein, and the vital-organ proteome shows no enrichment. Missing: any dependency (DepMap is non-selective), antibody validation and tumour heterogeneity; this is a data-ranked hypothesis, not a validated target.

The COL23A1 AlphaFold model is low confidence (mean pLDDT [gene=COL23A1; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=58.91]) and only a tiny shallow cavity was found, so there is no small-molecule structural handle; an antibody route is the plausible modality. This heuristic does not exclude other modalities.

RAB42 (tumour track): RCC cells hold this share of its tumour transcripts [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627]; it is up in TCGA and purity-robust with no survival signal and no clinical drug. Its surface call is unknown, so antibody accessibility is not established, and there is no dependency evidence.

OLFML2A (stroma track): fibroblasts hold this share of its tumour transcripts [gene=OLFML2A; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.647]. It is secreted, replicated in TCGA and purity-robust with few ccrcc papers, but vital-organ expression (colon) is a safety question and no functional or dependency evidence exists.

JAG2 (stroma track): endothelium holds this share of its tumour transcripts [gene=JAG2; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.487], so the signal is split and only partly endothelial. It is a surface protein, replicated and purity-robust with a modest effect, but already has a non-trivial ccrcc literature and heart expression; endothelial specificity and function are unproven.

MILR1 (immune track): macrophage-derived surface protein with no ccrcc papers and no clinical drug, adverse prognosis in TCGA, but flagged as infiltration-driven because its fold change in a pure tumour shrinks to [gene=MILR1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.414]. It is a macrophage-targeting hypothesis whose tumour-up signal reflects infiltration, with no dependency data.

LILRB4 (immune track): macrophage surface receptor with no clinical drug listed, but infiltration-driven (fold change in a pure tumour only [gene=LILRB4; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.508]) and its TCGA survival association is not significant. It is a microenvironment hypothesis with lung expression as a safety question.

GAL3ST4 (immune track): macrophage enzyme, replicated and with adverse TCGA survival, and the fold change in a pure tumour is small [gene=GAL3ST4; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.401]. It is a Golgi (internal) protein, so not antibody-accessible, and lacks any functional validation.

caveats: Single-cell attribution comes from twelve donors; endothelium and fibroblast groups come from few donors, so shares are uncertain.
Transcript share depends on how many cells of each type were captured; cpm_share was used as a cross-check.
Structural-context scores are monomer heuristics and do not identify degrons, ligase compatibility or degradation.
Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses: no dependency or functional evidence, literature counted by gene symbol.
CD70 single-cell rows had no evidence ids, so its expression is described in words only.
MET and EGFR were not examined within the tool budget.
ALDOB, SLC22A8, UMOD, FABP1 and NPHS2 in the convergence top ten are tumour-down (normal kidney) biomarkers, not tumour-cell targets, and were not profiled at single-cell level.
